newsitem.title: LEBANON: Solidere shares rise further in Beirut.
newsitem.headline: Solidere shares rise further in Beirut.

text.p: Solidere shares continued rising on the Beirut Stock Exchange on Friday and dealers said the upward trend might signal a rotation of funds from banks to Lebanon's biggest company.
Prices of two out of the three bank shares listed on the BSE were unchanged on Friday.

"Banks are getting more and more stable so we might witness a rotation of funds from the traditional profit centres to Solidere," Nicholas Sawan, Deputy Manager, head of trading at Beirut finance house Lebanon Invest said.
Solidere A and B shares closed at $11 from $10.5 and $10.875 respectively. Dealers said the rise, begun on Tuesday, was stimulated by a surge of the company's Global Depositary Receipts in London.
"The upward trend would definitely continue in the coming week," Sawan told Reuters.
The rise ended a prolonged period during which the shares have stagnated close to their historic lows.

The GDRs, issued last November at $11.5, soared on the London Stock Exchange on Tuesday to $17.625 from last week's $12 and the company said purchases by U.S. and European emerging market funds were behind the increase. The GDRs traded at $16 on Friday.
Dealers said the GDR rise in addition to a Merril Lynch report that valued Solidere shares at $20 awakened people's minds that the shares were trading at huge discounts in Beirut.

Demand for A and B shares on Friday's first fixing totalled 265,006 shares against a supply of 115,979. This compared with demand of 252,788 againt a supply of 124,736 on Wednesday and 75,022 shares against 110,665 on Tuesday.
Financial markets closed on Thursday for the Labour Day holiday.
The LIBX bank index rose 0.25 percent to 138.04. The BLOM general index rose 2.69 percent to 953.96 and the LISPI fell 0.58 percent to 87.01.
Of the three listed banks, only Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce rose to $16.625 from $16.5. A block of 1,500 BLC shares traded on the floor at $16.75.
Banque Audi held steady at $20.125 and Bank of Beirut was unchanged at $3.5625.
Total BSE turnover was 273,095 shares against Wednesday's 298,316 and value was $2,953,042 against $2,667,156.
Three of the four listed industrials were traded. Ciments Blancs, trading for the first time in more than two weeks, fell to $5 from $5.5 on turnover of 800 shares.
Pipemaker Eternit fell slightly to $1.8125 from $1.8750 while Ciments Libanais held steady at $1.2812.
